pathway.question: How do provisional ratings and funding conditions change the published liquidity plan?

View: As of 11 April 2024, Ford Otomotiv Sanayi A.S. / Ford Otosan's published liquidity plan supported conditional ordinary refinancing, not completed funding. Removing either planned source leaves only a small nominal buffer; removing both produces a deficit. Adding the unstressed dividend also produces a deficit despite retaining both sources. Fresh CP-2H therefore changes the funding inference: preliminary/expected note ratings and adequate/comfortable liquidity opinions cannot substitute for placement, usable proceeds, documentation and operating performance.

CP-2H's rating distinctions materially constrain reliance on CP-2G. S&P's issuer rating was preliminary BB- with a Positive outlook, and its proposed unsecured-note rating was preliminary BB-; finalisation required successful issuance, satisfactory final documentation and operating performance consistent with its base case. Material departures could lead to revision or withdrawal. Fitch's BB+/Stable issuer rating was published, but its proposed-note BB+(EXP)/RR4 remained expected and conditional on refinancing completion and conforming documents. Neither rating status proves settlement. Their two-symbol-step difference establishes neither a pricing advantage nor default/LME intent. (S pp.1,3 L173–182; F pp.1–2 L5–8,153–166.)

The proposed up-to-USD500 million parent unsecured bond serves general corporate purposes, including strategic capex and refinancing short debt. The EUR435 million Romanian subsidiary facility was signed in March 2024 for capex. These are distinct currencies, borrowers and purposes; the TRY amounts are S&P's approximate translations, not this module's FX conversions. Signing alone does not prove unconditional availability, upstream transferability or eligibility to meet parent maturities. Draw conditions, eligible expenditure, use controls and local covenant compliance must be checked. (S p.1 L173–179; M p.2 L475–517.)

The single-source cases retain nominal coverage but little room for weaker cash FFO, a delayed draw or intra-year mismatch. The combined deficit identifies the amount of unresolved annual funding need under those assumptions; it does not identify which payment would fail first. An annual surplus cannot establish daily cash adequacy. S&P identifies short maturities and absence of a long-term committed RCF as limitations. Fitch's EUR100 million working-capital revolver and expected rolling short-term renewals are supportive, but cannot be added as unverified incremental cash. (M p.2 L479–499; F p.2 L126–135.)

CP-2G's improving leverage ratio is earnings-led, not debt repayment: its adjusted debt rises across both forecast years. CP-2H also preserves Fitch's approximate around-2x net-leverage outlook versus the strict above-2.0x-by-2025 sensitivity; an exact breach or buffer is not established. S&P gross leverage cannot fill that gap. Romanian hard-currency cash matters separately: reported earnings growth will not protect creditors if collections are unusable for foreign debt service and imports. (Supplied CP-2G/CP-2H; S p.3 L184–202; F pp.1–2 L94–124.)

Fitch's April 2024 expectation places most term loan Bs and the planned bond in a conditional 2026–28 maturity cluster after refinancing. This would ease nearer-term needs while concentrating later refinancing risk; it is not a complete maturity wall or an upcoming-2026 monitoring assertion made with later knowledge. Exact dates, amortisation and executed tenor are Not supplied. (F p.2 L133–135.)

The strongest contrary case is ordinary investment-cycle funding supported by contractual volumes, cost-plus expense recovery and capex recovery over the product cycle, rapid hard-currency collections and strategic importance to FMC. Dividend reductions have historical precedent; spending flexibility may bridge the investment trough. This countercase wins if closing evidence and executable draws arrive before uses, protected volumes become collected usable cash, Romanian ramp economics hold, and distributions/spending adjust before buffers disappear. Contract protection is not a corporate debt guarantee: Fitch notes absent debt guarantees/cross-default and does not apply its potential parent uplift. (M p.1 L24–39,51–80; S p.1 L135–158.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amounts are TRY billions and approximate in economic meaning. Decimal precision below reproduces K exactly; it does not improve source accuracy. Ratios are plain fractions to four decimals, not percentages. All cases use the same 2024 issuer-group analytical period, while facility fungibility remains unverified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: K p.1 retains actual fresh offline calls of unchanged total/difference/ratio functions, independently Fraction-checked with source-literal verification. These retained outputs are consumed here, not represented as new model tool calls. No new calculations were required.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The source trace is cash 15.2 plus cash FFO 63 plus planned bond 16 plus capex facility 15, giving 109.2. Uses are maturities 33.8, working capital 8.6, the full up-to-2 extra swing and unstressed reported capex 46.3, giving 90.7. Difference means sources minus uses; ratio means sources divided by strictly positive uses. Each sensitivity changes only the named component. The dividend overlay uses 27.1; the capex illustration applies exactly 15% to 46.3. (M p.2 L484–505; K p.1.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The resulting approximately 1.2x reproduces rounded components, not S&P's undisclosed exact liquidity model. Cash FFO 63 is not replaced with adjusted financial-summary FFO 48.717; reported capex 46.3 is not replaced with adjusted capex. S&P cash 15.2 is not replaced with Fitch restricted-adjusted available cash 5.0. Their reconciliation is Not supplied. The liquidity use list excludes committed dividends under potential stress even though its capex amount is unstressed; the separate overlay deliberately changes that dividend assumption. No conditional nominal excess establishes unrestricted liquidity, distribution capacity or legal borrowing capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Full maturity wall, operative terms, exact covenant headroom, recovery and full financing approval are Not supplied. S&P reports consolidated EBRD/IFC and Romanian-local 3.5x tests with different perimeters, and no financial covenants on the proposed bond; those descriptions are not operative-document verification. Headroom is Not calculable without matching definitions, operands and certificates. Subsidiary debt introduces structural-priority questions; S&P's approximately 20% pro-forma priority ratio and Fitch RR4 do not provide a legal waterfall or independently modelled recovery. (M pp.2–3 L506–546.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upstream -1/+1 TRY-million display residuals remain unresolved and unchanged; they are not plugged into this rounded liquidity bridge. Exact cash availability, monthly sequencing, financing fees and executable spending cuts remain missing. No actual failure, subsequent rating action, realised forecast outcome or LME proposal is established. Other output artifacts are Not supplied. Handoff checking does not certify underwriting, legal capacity or full module acceptance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CP-4 should verify final note/facility terms, draw and use restrictions, covenant definitions, guarantees and subsidiary priority before instrument-specific decisions. CP-2D/CP-2G should supply dated cash sequencing and matching cash-flow definitions; CP-2H receives execution/performance evidence without cross-agency metric substitution. CP-6 receives both the funding-dependency conclusion and the strongest ordinary-funding countercase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CP-OS retains the execution loop. Any separate delivery must reuse this exact accepted handoff, not rebuild the analysis or produce Excel. This is the fresh scoped CP-3C ratings-to-funding consumption; it does not approve full refinancing, liability management, recovery or security selection. Further outcomes require a separate dated authorization.
